fatal_errors: The proposed material is conventional tempered martensitic steel rather than the AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic high-entropy alloy sought in the stated context.
The hypothesis substitutes classical impurity-segregation temper embrittlement for the target mechanism involving L12 ordering and jagged FCC/B2 phase boundaries.
It conflates thermal aging temperature with mechanical testing temperature; the target transition is produced by distinct aging treatments, particularly near 600°C and 750°C.
The claim that the steel is ductile at low temperature is not generally valid and conflicts with the conventional ductile-to-brittle transition of many ferritic/martensitic steels.
explanation: The response reproduces only the generic idea of a non-monotonic ductility change. It misses the central finding: as-cast FCC+B2 AlCoCrFeNi2.1 develops minimum ductility after aging near 600°C because enhanced L12 ordering raises APBE/modulus and promotes planar slip while jagged B2/FCC boundary tips concentrate stress; ductility returns near 750°C as ordering is reduced and ductile boundary transition zones form. Conventional impurity-segregated steel is the comparison baseline, not the requested material. Although the proposed tensile, fractography, and segregation measurements could test its own steel hypothesis, they do not discriminate the target phase-boundary/order mechanism.
